Una dintre noi a murit

Jeneva Rose, Casandra Caia-Facaș (Translator)

3.81
169,269 ratings17,005 reviews
Rate this book
Prieteniile pot fi complicate – dar nimeni nu se aștepta ca ele să fie letale!

Femeile din Buckhead au tot ce și-ar putea dori: diamante, proprietăți impresionante cu garderobe pe măsură și nu în ultimul rând, un salon de lux, care își deschide porțile doar celor mai influente nume din înalta societate.

Însă atunci când una dintre cliente este găsită fără suflare, secretele întregii clientele riscă să iasă la iveală, zguduind elita din Buckhead cu povești scandaloase despre putere, sex și trădare. Cine va supraviețui intrigilor și cine va cădea pradă jocului puterii?

Shannon – fosta „regină” a lumii mondene din Buckhead, ajunsă pe punctul de a-și pierde statutul, după ce soțul politician o înlocuiește cu o femeie cu mult mai tânără...

Crystal – noua soție, o tânără inocentă din Texas, nepregătită să ia locul lui Shannon și să înfrunte toate obstacolele clasei de vârf...

Olivia – după ani în care a așteptat în tăcere căderea lui Shannon, Olivia este pregătită să taie și să spânzure pentru a ajunge în lumina reflectoarelor...

Karen – un agent imobiliar de succes, cu un secret care i-ar putea distruge familia și cariera...

Jenny – proprietara salonului, cunoaște cele mai mari secrete ale clientelor sale. Și tăcerea ei nu poate fi cumpărată atât de ușor...

Descoperă un thriller seducător și plin de suspans care îmbină tensiunea din Marile minciuni nevinovate și atmosfera din Neveste disperate.

HAPPY PUBLICATION DAY!

Out of all the “housewife” thrillers I’ve read, this one features the most deliciously evil villain!

The women of Buckhead are known for being plastic/beautiful, wealthy, and downright vicious.

Shannon has always been the most powerful woman of Buckhead…until now. Her politician husband, Bryce, divorces her and remarries a younger woman. Shannon is used goods.

Olivia has been dying to be the queen bee-yotch for years, and finally gets her chance now that Shannon isn’t married to a powerful man. Olivia will do anything to be on top, and doesn’t care who gets hurt along the way.

Crystal is the younger woman who marries Blake. She came from Texas and has never been around wealth. Just wait until she sees what she’s dealing with.

Karen works hard for what she has, and is the only one with both a husband and child. If only life in Buckhead could be peaceful, but that’s not going to happen with this group.

Jenny owns a salon that all of the women are serviced at. Just like a bartender or cab driver, she’s privy to plenty of tantalizing secrets.

Too bad some of these secrets will get someone killed.

This was an absolute blast to read. Some of the characters are so atrocious and wickedly deceiving. There are also some I rooted for. The biting dialogue is darkly humorous with plenty of snark and bitchiness. There are so many juicy secrets and threads, some of them downright cringeworthy in the best way. The different POVs are successful in building suspense, and the delectable ending is absolutely perfect for these folks!

This is definitely a popcorn thriller 🍿, and so well done at that. I loved it, and look forward to reading more from this author.

4.5 stars.

**3.5-stars rounded up**

Jenny is the owner of a posh salon in the upscale area of Buckhead in Atlanta. Her salon, Glow, caters to a set number of wealthy clients who come in for very regular treatments.

Because of this exclusivity and frequency of visits, Jenny has come to know her clients very, very well. Almost too well for her tastes. Along with her assistant, Jenny has become quite versed in navigating the ups-and-downs of her clients toxic relationships.



The most recent drama involves former Queen Bee, Shannon, whose politician husband, Bryce Madison, recently left her for a 20-something waitress he met while on a business trip to Texas.

The waitress, Crystal, has recently moved to town and become the new Mrs. Madison. Young and innocent, like Dorothy walking into Oz, Crystal has no idea what she is in for when it comes to Buckhead society.



For her part, Olivia is all too happy to sit back and watch Shannon's demise. Truthfully, she's been waiting for that star to fall for a while. As she sees it, now is her time.

Lastly, there's Karen. The least aggressive socially of the bunch, Karen's still hiding some big secrets of her own.



These women are used to a constant state of drama, with under-handed insults being slung back and forth, but how far are they willing to take it? Would someone actually kill to protect their position in the community? How about to keep their secrets secret?

Y'all, somebody is not going to make it out alive...



One of Us is Dead is like Fried Green Tomatoes met The Real Housewives of Atlanta, they fell in love and had a baby that was essentially an Adult version of Mean Girls.

You know based off that description that my evil a$$ is 100% here for it.



I had the pleasure of listening to the audiobook for this one, which does feature a full cast. It was really well done and I definitely recommend that format.

It was fun having a different narrator for each perspective. It felt like I was really getting to know these characters and they are twisted. Everyone was hiding something. Everyone knew things they shouldn't. They were just all up in each others business. It was captivating.



I did have a lot of fun with this and became invested quickly. It was really close to a full 4-stars for me. I was disappointed that the ending wrapped everything up so quickly though.

I wanted more intrigue as far as the murdery bits were concerned. For most of the narrative I actually forgot that the whole point was that someone was ultimately going to end up dead. There was so little focus on that.

I would have appreciated more time invested in those aspects, but of course, that is completely a personal taste issue. I was just sort of hoping for a wee more mystery.



Overall, this is a super fun, fast-paced, dramatic and slightly ridiculous read.

Be forewarned, however, if you are not into girl-on-girl slander, back-stabbing and crime, this may not be for you. Just know going in these women are brutal. They aren't holding any punches.



Thank you so much to the publisher, Blackstone Publishing, for providing me with a copy to read and review. I had a ton of fun with this one!

I had fun with it, got my nails done, and didn't take it too seriously!

"The women dressed up in their most expensive gowns, trying to outdo one another. The men wrote large checks to compensate for other areas in which they were lacking"- Welcome to Buckhead, Atlanta.

❤ ✔ — Thank you to Laura for this recommendation. It did not disappoint.

✨Six entitled women acting unhinged…sign me up. Buckle up for a wild ride of drama, gossip, backstabbing, and cattiness! If you ever indulged in some good old Real Housewives/ Desperate Housewives type of TV, then you will likely enjoy this book. Add in a murder and you have a highly entertaining story that I really enjoyed. This was over the top, crazy, wild, and just completely ridiculous and I loved every page of it.✨

“The truth is, I’d rather be dead than poor, and the easiest way to stay rich is to stay powerful”

The Plot- One of the main female characters is dead. But why and who? A salon owner who serves the rich housewives of Buckhead recalls the events that led up to the death of one of them. She is the one that knows these ladies on a different level. These ladies come to her to get all dolled up and spill their secrets to her because she is just “the help” who is she going to tell? The salon owner knows everyone of their demons and their deep, darkest secrets. With sex, lies, betrayal amongst the group of friends it could be anyone.

✂️ Side note: when I go to the hair salon I talk to most shit and have the time of my life with my hairdresser. So it was very realistic to me that the hairdresser knew all the secrets ✂️

“Your skin is glowing, I can barely notice the lack of elasticity today”

The Characters- The women of Buckhead are known for being plastic/beautiful, wealthy, and downright vicious.

Jenny- The salon owner and the peacemaker.

Olivia-I hated this chick from the very first introduction. She was the queen bee of the group. The one hungry for power and she will do anything for it. She is the typical rich mean women. I kept picturing the step-mom from parent trap LMAO

Shannon- The scorned ex- wife. I love this crazy bi***. She was so delulu it was hilarious. Omg she had me dying laughing but also cringing with the shit she pulled. We love an unhinged funny chick.

Crystal- The new girl in town and the new wife. Ahh so she was the other woman. Even tho she stole Shannon husband I grew to like her very quickly. She was smart and witty.

Karen- She was a breath of fresh air. She didn’t fit into this group of caddy ladies but she was definitely needed for the groups dynamic.

Keisha- Jenny’s best friend/ coworker. She was a hot ticket.

“The men in our lives dont define us. We define ourselves”

The Writing & Pace- One of Us is Dead is told using alternating points of view and an alternating timeline. The timeline alternates between before the murder and after the murder. You don't know who dies until the very end so the majority of the book is drama leading up to it. This was a fast paced story.

“Women weren’t meant to be quiet.”

My Thoughts- Thoroughly captivating and engaging, this story was one that left me reeling at the end with all the twists and turns.I am a huge fan of rich-person drama, so I was sold right from the description. The drama and cattiness of these women was so fun to read, and I couldn’t wait to find out who was dead and why. My jaw was on the floor at the end of this book. Honey! I was like damnn haha

“& in this town it’s all about who you know, what you wear, how you look, and how much money and power you have”

This was like desperate housewives on crack! I had to laugh when I read their book club read and discussed Vogue. Who does that? These ladies do!

These women did not save that drama for their mama, that is for sure! Oh, how deliciously devious and spoiled these women were.

Shannon-divorced when her husband met a younger woman. Of course, she is angry, hurt, and bitter. On top of that her ex-husband's new wife is in her social circle.

Crystal- the new young beautiful wife who married Shannon's ex-husband.

Olivia - is cruel, meal and hides behind “just kidding" when she is nasty to others. It is her mission to bring down Shannon.

Jenny - owns an exclusive spa and knows all of the ladies’ secrets.

Karen - is married with a child. Yet, she yearns for something else.

All these women have secrets. All want to protect their secrets. How far will anyone go to protect their secret. That is the question.

So juicy, so much fun, so full of petty backstabbing and cruel comments. I could not stop listening This was such a fun book/audio book. The narrators did such an amazing job. I didn't want to turn it off.

I highly recommend the audiobook. I was aghast at some of their antics. Others I felt for. I had some eye rolling moments! This was such a fun guilty pleasure! I have to say this was one of my favorite audiobooks so far this year!

Do yourself a favor and join in the fun by picking up this book.

Spoiled. Privileged. Devious. Deadly.

Highly Recommend.

TRIGGER WARNING: all they do is drink in this book. Sometimes they consume more alcohol than humanly possible.

I can’t even begin to say how horrible this book was. The ONLY chapters that matter are chapters 84 & 85. That’s just the last 10 pages of the book y’all.

This book is an assault on all women. Every character is vapid and stupid, caricatures of RH in any area. Women are NOT this stupid.

They reference people who work in the mansions and at the parties as “The Help” nearly a dozen times. Are you fucking kidding me?

The 1 🌟 comes from the trope of knowing someone is dead and NOT disclosing it until the end.

It won’t be a surprise though. You’ll know immediately who is dead.

The immature, catty, selfish bullshit never stops. This book is FULL OF REPETITION. It wasn’t character development as it was hammering 🔨 it in our heads all the characters’ traits ad Nauseam.

For a book that is less than 300 pages, it took an inordinate amount of time to read. The pages are cringeworthy and useless. The timeline is difficult to assess as it jumps from POVs (and they all sound like the same woman so y’all won’t even remember who is speaking) and time frames without notice.

Lots of closed captioned writing that provides useless content to fill the pages. Everything is predictable. The dialogue is laughable and the women are pitiful.

The problem is … they really aren’t stupid, but you won’t know that until the end. By then you won’t care.

I devoured this one in a few hours, it's gripping, full of twists, unhinged and has complex characters. I loved that the hairdresser was the centre-point of the story because we all talk trash when we are getting our hair done 💇‍♀️

I love this kind of drama so I found it funny and didn't take it too seriously. Most of the story is centred around the drama rather than the actual crime so keep that in mind. I did expect a bit more from the ending because it wrapped up quite quickly but I still enjoyed it.

Let me introduce you to the ladies:

Jenny - The hairdresser and the heart of the story. We see Jenny in both the flashbacks and in the current timeline throughout the story.

Olivia - Olivia is married to Dean but her single most important thing in life is herself. Olivia reminds me of Bree from desperate housewives because she's the pact leader and a little dominatrix. I actually liked Bree though, she was iconic. Olivia is the shein version.

Shannon - Is a long term resident and bitter ex wife of Bryce. She's probably a little 🤪 but I loved her. I aspire to be her level of delusional.

Crystal - Crystal is Bryce's new younger wife and new in town. I was expecting to dislike her given the narrative this type of character has but she was a queen 💅

Karen- Is a little wallflower and is married to Mark. She's not your typical suburban housewife.

Keisha - She is a beautician at the salon so she has an insight to what's divulged by the local ladies. She's a fun addition to the antics but we didn't get her POV.

EXCERPT: Jenny - present

'I've spent thousands of hours working on these women. I've primped, waxed, cut, painted, spray-painted, powdered and massaged them. I know almost every inch of their bodies. But I also know their demons - their deepest, darkest secrets. The things we try to bury beneath the surface so as not to show the world the doppelganger lurking within us. So, am I surprised something like this happened? Not in the slightest . . . '

ABOUT 'ONE OF US IS DEAD': Meet the women of Buckhead—a place of expensive cars, huge houses, and competitive friendships.

Shannon was once the queen bee of Buckhead. But she’s been unceremoniously dumped by Bryce, her politician husband. When Bryce replaces her with a much younger woman, Shannon sets out to take revenge …

Crystal has stepped into Shannon’s old shoes. A young, innocent Texan girl, she simply has no idea what she’s up against …

Olivia has waited years to take Shannon’s crown as the unofficial queen of Buckhead. Finally, her moment has come. But to take her rightful place, she will need to use every backstabbing, manipulative, underhand trick in the book …

Jenny owns Glow, the most exclusive salon in town. Jenny knows all her clients’ secrets and darkest desires. But will she ever tell?

Who amongst these women will be clever enough to survive Buckhead—and who will wind up dead? They say that friendships can be complex, but no one said it could ever be this deadly.

MY THOUGHTS: Every now and then I like to read a novel about bitchy women, but One of Us is Dead takes this to a whole new level, and after the initial enjoyment, I'm afraid my enthusiasm began to wane to the point where I was toying with the idea of quitting this read. But then . . . something very unexpected happened that again, briefly, piqued my interest enough to carry me through to the end.

I think that if you are a fan of the 'Real Housewives' programmes you will probably love this. The women have all married wealthy men. They are mostly various degrees of spoiled, sculpted, plastic, back-stabbing bitches. They spend their time in the beauty salon, lunching, shopping, drinking, entertaining and organising charity fundraisers, which probably would have benefited more had they just donated their collection of Birkin bags. But murder? That's not what these ladies, and I use the term very loosely, do. Their weapons are usually their tongues, not baseball bats and Glocks.

There are a few things that annoyed me: the build up is very long compared to the rather quick resolution; and the very unexpected happening seems to get lost in the story until the very end and there doesn't seem to be any legal ramifications or investigation. This is a big issue!

I did love the cast of narrators in the audio version, each character having their own voice. I read/listened to One of Us is Dead and vastly preferred the audiobook.

There is a definite market for this book and I do wish I had enjoyed it more.

⭐⭐⭐.3

Meet Buckhead, the town where housewives behave at their worst and murder is the special of the day.

The group of women included:

Olivia: she is egocentric and will do anything to be on top. She has waited years to help destroyed Shannon now that she is down on her luck.

Shannon: once the most powerful woman in town, married to Bryce, the rich politician until her marriage falls apart and he leaves her for a younger woman whom he marries.

Crystal: a young woman from Texas and now the wife of Bryce.

Karen: a very successful real state agent. She is married to a successful plastic surgeon and has a small child.

Jenny: the owner of Glow. The IT beauty salon. The place where these women backstab each other, drink champagne and tell their secrets intend it or not.

I had so much fun listening/reading this one. The women were catty, spoiled, and plastic but entertaining nonetheless. The audio narrators Andi Arndt, Hillary Huber, Elizabeth Evans, Brittany Pressley, and Cassandra Campbell did a wonderful job at fleshing out these women for me. I will say Jenny was my favorite since she was the most down-to-earth person in the group. I did root for almost all of them through the book.

After finishing listening to this guilty pleasure, I know I will read Jeneva Rose's next book.

Cliffhanger: No

“Don’t let them fool you, Detective. Individually, they’re genuine and they can be kind ... but when you put them in a room together, these women are downright toxic.”
I picked up One of Us Is Dead because it’s gotten really good reviews from a lot of GR friends whose opinions I usually agree with. But, wow, am I an outlier here. To process my thoughts, I think it’d be helpful to break down the pros and cons of this novel.

Pros:
The title: One of Us Is Dead is a completely accurate title. The story is told from the perspective of five different first-person narrators, and one of them is dead by the end of the book. Some book titles lie (why yes, I am still bothered by The Perks of Being a Wallflower), but this book is not one of them.

The cover: That is an eye-catching cover.

Cons:
Characters: I don’t watch the Real Housewives series, so I don’t know how much these women behave like those women. But almost all of the characters in One of Us Is Dead are just the worst. Shannon, reeling from her recent divorce from Bryce the Congressman, is delusional about her current situation. Karen, the one who literally thinks she “not like the other wives,” is clueless about her current situation. Crystal, Bryce’s new wife, is the most perceptive and tolerable character but she’s clearly hiding something about her past from the reader. Which brings us to Olivia ….

Olivia: Olivia may be the most vile character I’ve ever read. Cruella de Vil is more nuanced and believable. Olivia has zero redeeming qualities, holds irrational grudges, and is so awful to the people she considers her friends that I simply refuse to believe that anyone would spend a moment of time with her. Still, a book with unlikeable characters can still be great (Lolita and Gone Girl are just two examples). Unlikeable characters were not my only problem with this novel, which leads us to ….

Story: In the present, a police detective is interviewing Jenny, the owner of an upscale salon where a surprising amount of the story takes place. There’s been a murder, but the reader isn’t told who’s dead until the book is almost over. Most of the book is told in flashbacks from the perspective of the five narrators that slowly reveal their connections and interactions, providing lots of options for the identity of both the killer and the victim. So, if you’ve seen or read Big Little Lies, One of Us Is Dead will feel really familiar. There are all of these references to death and murder throughout the story (“he was going to be the death of me,” “you’re going to have a killer time,” things like that), but they aren’t actually clues about who’s going to die. It could have been clever foreshadowing if there was less of it, and if the book was not literally called One of Us Is Dead. You might figure out who the murder victim will be (I did), but pretty much every character is given a motive to be both killer and victim. There are several twists and reveals during the story that were completely predictable … until the ending.

Ending: There’s something completely unpredictable going on under the surface of the story. But once it’s revealed it felt wildly out of place. Worse, when the murder is finally explained, the explanation does not hold up to scrutiny. It simply does not make sense physically or logistically.

Conclusion:
There’s a character who at one point complains that she’s sick of these characters’ “bullshit and pointless rivalries.” I could not have agreed more. If it wasn’t for the knowledge that there was going to be a murder, I don’t know why anyone would care about these toxic frenemies. And even if someone loves books about this particular type of desperate housewife, I’d still say One of Us Is Dead is deeply flawed. This book is a hard stay away for me, but feel free to take my opinion with a mountain of salt. Like I said at the start, my negative opinion is clearly in the minority here.

Grab your champagne and your sharpest stilettos - Jeneva Rose's "One of Us Is Dead" is a deliciously wicked dive into the backstabbing world of Atlanta's elite! Think "Real Housewives" meets "Big Little Lies" with an extra shot of murder, and you've got this absolutely addictive thriller that had me canceling plans just to keep reading.

The story revolves around the most exclusive salon in Buckhead, Atlanta, where the city's elite wives come to gossip, scheme, and maintain their perfect facades. At the center of this viper's nest is Shannon Thomas, the queen bee whose social reign seems unshakeable - until Jenny McCallister arrives in town. Jenny, the beautiful new wife of Shannon's ex-husband, threatens to upset the careful balance of power, and suddenly the salon becomes a battlefield where alliances shift as quickly as seasonal fashion trends.

Rose masterfully orchestrates her cast of characters: there's Crystal, the salon owner who knows everyone's dirty secrets; Karen, desperate to maintain her social standing; Shannon, the dethroned queen ready to strike back; and Jenny, the newcomer who might not be as naive as she appears. Each woman's voice is distinct and compelling, making you simultaneously root for and suspect them all.

The structure is brilliantly crafted, with multiple POVs and timeline shifts that keep you guessing. We know from the start that someone ends up dead, but Rose keeps you on your toes about both the victim and the killer. The tension builds exquisitely as secrets unravel, alliances crumble, and perfectly manicured claws come out.

What makes this book particularly engaging is how Rose balances the glittering surface of wealth and social status with the darkness lurking underneath. The petty rivalries and social climbing serve as perfect cover for deeper, deadlier motivations. The author nails the atmosphere of high-society Atlanta, where appearances are everything and social death can be worse than actual murder - until, of course, real murder enters the picture.

The dialogue crackles with wit and venom - these women weaponize words like master fencers, and every conversation is a duel. I found myself highlighting countless passages of perfectly crafted shade and savage one-liners. Rose has a particular talent for showing how these women use politeness as a weapon and social niceties as armor.

The mystery itself is cleverly plotted, with enough red herrings to keep you guessing but playing completely fair with the clues. When the final revelations come, they're both shocking and satisfying, making you want to go back and spot all the breadcrumbs you missed.

"One of Us Is Dead" is more than just a murder mystery - it's a razor-sharp satire of social climbing, a meditation on power and privilege, and a reminder that sometimes the most dangerous weapon isn't a knife or gun, but a carefully placed rumor at a salon chair.

This book is absolutely perfect for fans of domestic suspense who like their thrillers with a heavy dose of social commentary and dark humor. It's "Mean Girls" grown up and gone terribly, deliciously wrong. Jeneva Rose has created something special here - a thriller that manages to be both wickedly entertaining and smartly observant of human nature.

Five perfectly polished stars for this gloriously twisted tale of beauty, betrayal, and murder. Just remember - in Buckhead, even the deadliest poison comes in a designer bottle!

Love me a juicy adults behaving badly thriller! Five entitled women living in the affluent suburb of Buckhead in Georgia. Shannon, the wronged first wife. Crystal, the fresh faced naïve second wife. Olivia, the villain you will love to hate. Karen, the voice of reason. And Jenny, the salon owner who knows all these lady’s secrets. From the title of the book you know someone will be dead by the end. What you don’t know is who,, how and why. Everyone is so entangled, Seriously everyone has a good reason to want to kill everyone else. These ladies were all so petty, vapid and fun to read about. The story is told from the POV of each of these five women. I loved how we got to get inside the head of each of these characters and see what made them tick. The audiobook was narrated by an all-star cast of five amazing narrators who brought each of these characters to life. If you are an audiobook person then I 10/10 recommend this on audio. It is probably one of the best I’ve listened to this year. Looking forward to reading even more from Jeneva Rose.

This book in emojis: 💅🏻 💁🏻‍♀️ 🍷 💍 🦌

*** Big thank you to Blackstone Publishing for my gifted copy of this book. All opinions are my own. ***

(3.5 stars). I will start off by saying that this was a fun, entertaining, and fast read. However, if I was 10 or 20 years younger I would have definitely enjoyed it more.
One Of Us Is Dead consists of a bunch of rich, catty, manipulative women who I didn’t care much about. I’m at the age where I try to stay away from the drama, let alone read about it.

There were a few of the women characters who I did like, and I’m glad that they got their redemption in the end. Also, if you’ve read the synopsis of the book and the title, you will know that someone does end up dead in this story. All I have to say is Thank God it was the right one or else I would have thrown this book out the window!!

Along with the female drama, there were some twists thrown in there that gave this book a bit of suspense. I also really enjoyed the ending. Was it unrealistic? Maybe. But, because of it I gave this book a higher rating.

I previously read and loved The Perfect Marriage by Jeneva Rose, and I look forward to reading whatever she comes up with next!
